sections.heading: Glossary term: Quasar
sections.body: Short for quasi-stellar radio source, quasars are distant extragalactic sources. Quasars appear as stars (hence, quasi-stellar) and were initially detected with radio telescopes. Observations reveal that they are associated with the region around the most massive supermassive black holes at the center of galaxies. Quasars are a subclass of active galactic nuclei (AGN), which includes radio and Seyfert galaxies, blazars, and low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs). Quasars can be as much as 100 times more luminous than their host galaxy. Some also have giant jets which interact with the gas around and within their host galaxy. Because of their high luminosities, quasars can be used to study distant galaxies, intervening galaxies, and the intergalactic medium. 3C 273 was the first quasar detected.

Glossary term: Quasar

Also known as quasi-stellar object (QSO)

Description: Short for quasi-stellar radio source, quasars are distant extragalactic sources. Quasars appear as stars (hence, quasi-stellar) and were initially detected with radio telescopes. Observations reveal that they are associated with the region around the most massive supermassive black holes at the center of galaxies. Quasars are a subclass of active galactic nuclei (AGN), which includes radio and Seyfert galaxies, blazars, and low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs). Quasars can be as much as 100 times more luminous than their host galaxy. Some also have giant jets which interact with the gas around and within their host galaxy. Because of their high luminosities, quasars can be used to study distant galaxies, intervening galaxies, and the intergalactic medium. 3C 273 was the first quasar detected.

Related Terms:

  • Active Galactic Nucleus
  • Black Hole
  • Radio Astronomy


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. You can find a full list of credits here. All glossary terms and their definitions are released under a Creative Commons CC BY-4.0 license and should be credited to "IAU OAE".

sections.body_ru: Сокращение от квазизвёздный радиоисточник; квазары — это далёкие внегалактические источники. Квазары выглядят как звёзды (отсюда «квазизвёздные») и были первоначально обнаружены с помощью радиотелескопов. Наблюдения показывают, что они связаны с областью вокруг самых массивных сверхмассивных чёрных дыр в центрах галактик. Квазары являются подклассом активных ядер галактик (AGN), который включает радиогалактики и сейфертовские галактики, блазары и области с низкоионизованными линиями излучения в ядрах (LINERs). Квазары могут быть до 100 раз ярче своей родительской галактики. Некоторые также имеют гигантские джеты, которые взаимодействуют с газом вокруг и внутри их родительской галактики. Благодаря высокой светимости квазары можно использовать для изучения далёких галактик, промежуточных галактик и межгалактической среды. 3C 273 был первым обнаруженным квазаром.
